beats.say: This animal has three hearts, and blue blood.
The common octopus. Eight arms, covered in suckers.
Two hearts pump blood through its gills. The third pumps it around the body.
And that third heart stops beating when it swims. So it would rather crawl.
Its blood is blue, because it's built on copper, not iron.
And most of its brain isn't even in its head.
Two-thirds of its nerve cells are in its arms.
Each arm can taste, touch, and move, all on its own.
It can change color in an instant, and even change the bumps on its skin.
Spray its ink in a predator's eyes, and it stings.
Its family is ancient. Its oldest known ancestor lived three hundred thirty million years ago.
Some octopuses even carry coconut shells around, to build a shelter.
One was reported sneaking into the next aquarium tank to steal fish.
But its life is short. Males die soon after mating.
And moms guard their eggs, then die after they hatch.
Here's the creepiest part. A cut-off arm can still react, even from a dead octopus.
Would you shake hands with one?
Three hearts, blue blood, and arms that keep going without it.
Follow me. Next, another animal that shouldn't exist.
